topic: Will we soon see the end of monocultures like wheat, maize, rice, and soy?
research_question: For production systems dominated by wheat, maize, rice, or soy, when do crop rotations, intercropping, varietal diversification, mixed farming, and neglected or underutilized crops improve food-supply stability and ecological services without unacceptable penalties in yield, income, nutrition, land use, water, or labor under climate and pest shocks?

candidate_routes.name: resilient_temporal_rotations
candidate_routes.reason: uses temporal complementarity, soil cover, nutrient cycling, and disease breaks

candidate_routes.name: spatial_intercropping_and_cultivar_mixtures
candidate_routes.reason: reduces synchronized susceptibility while testing competition and harvest cost

candidate_routes.name: genetic_and_landscape_insurance
candidate_routes.reason: combines cultivar diversity and habitat services for pest, pollination, and water regulation

candidate_routes.name: forgotten_crop_transition_corridors
candidate_routes.reason: links locally adapted crops to seed, processing, storage, nutrition, and markets

candidate_routes.name: shock_aware_food_system_portfolio
candidate_routes.reason: tests field and food-system resilience jointly under climate, pest, market, and trade shocks

candidate_routes.name: adoption_and_policy_co_design
candidate_routes.reason: tests whether risk-sharing and infrastructure make diversification persist

falsifiable_claims: portfolios reduce lower-tail loss under compound shocks
diversification mechanisms are complementary but not universally additive
field diversity does not guarantee food-system resilience
required_boundaries: dominant crops remain part of the transition portfolio
yield tonnes are not the only food metric
land-use displacement and food loss are explicit
